title: Learning to See China as China Sees Itself
gist: Podcast notes on Charles Gehrke's argument that Washington misreads Beijing's Taiwan motives: for China's leaders Taiwan is a political trauma tied to historical self-image, so deterrence built on American assumptions could fail.

insights.claim: Charles Gehrke argues US military planners may be misjudging Beijing's motives on Taiwan by treating it only as a strategic prize rather than, for China's leaders, an open wound tied to political trauma and national history.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: If Taiwan is driven by identity and history, cost-imposition logic may deter less than assumed.

insights.claim: Deterrence built on American assumptions about Chinese thinking could fail when it matters most; the US must first understand how China sees itself.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Tail risk for Taiwan Strait escalation is higher than models based on rational cost-benefit imply.
